actor: Government affairs policy lead, frontier AI developer advocating pre-release testing
job: Turning the 'sufficiently capable' ask into filed threshold language: a specific capability line plus a named cyber, biological and alignment battery.
outcome: Threshold text plus a named pre-release test entering a US federal rulemaking docket or a bill draft.
motivation: Having conceded the ban question, the pre-release gate is the only ask left, and an unwritten threshold binds nobody.

task.who: Frontier lab policy team, safety researchers and outside regulatory counsel
task.what: Draft capability-threshold and pre-release test language for filing
task.where: Federal rulemaking dockets and congressional staff drafting sessions
task.why: An unspecified threshold gates nothing and binds no release
task.how: Responsible scaling tiers, model cards, formal comment filings

actor: Committee counsel drafting AI legislation for a US congressional committee
job: Converting a contested capability threshold into statutory text: which releases the gate touches, who runs the battery, what trips it.
outcome: Introduced bill text carrying an explicit capability line and a named pre-release cyber, biological and alignment test.
motivation: An origin-keyed restriction cannot reach a domestic open-weight release, which leaves the capability-keyed line as the drafting option.

task.who: Committee counsel, legislative aides and legislative drafting staff
task.what: Write the capability threshold into bill text
task.where: Committee markups, hearings and legislative counsel drafts
task.why: Statutory text needs a line an agency can apply
task.how: Hearing testimony, agency technical assistance, stakeholder comment records

actor: Evaluation program staff at the US federal AI standards body
job: Specifying the cyber, biological and alignment evaluations a binding instrument can cite by name, and the capability levels that trigger them.
outcome: A published, citable federal test battery and tiering that rule text can incorporate by reference.
motivation: A rule cannot name a test that does not exist, and the toolkit for pacing the frontier is admittedly missing.

task.who: Federal AI standards evaluation staff and their national lab partners
task.what: Publish a referencable pre-release evaluation battery and tiers
task.where: Standards drafts, public comment periods and evaluation pilots
task.why: Instrument text can only name a test that exists
task.how: Red-team exercises, cyber ranges, uplift trials, alignment probes

actor: Policy director for the open-weights coalition of chip vendors, model publishers and foundations
job: Arguing where the capability line sits and who holds the pen, now that the coalition has conceded the ban question.
outcome: Comment filings and counter-drafts contesting threshold placement and test custody rather than the right to publish weights.
motivation: A line set too low turns every open-weight release into a gated one and hands the pen to a rival.

task.who: Coalition policy staff, member-company counsel and signatory technical leads
task.what: File counter-drafts contesting threshold placement and test custody
task.where: Federal comment dockets and coalition working groups
task.why: A low line would gate ordinary open-weight releases
task.how: Signatory bloc letters, docket comments, benchmarking rebuttals

actor: Specification editor at a multi-signatory frontier AI industry consortium
job: Assembling one spec text both camps will sign: a capability threshold, a named pre-release battery, and who administers it.
outcome: A signed multi-signatory industry specification carrying the threshold and the named cyber, biological and alignment test.
motivation: An industry spec can land before federal text does, and whoever ships first sets the line others argue against.

task.who: Consortium secretariat, member policy leads and the working group chair
task.what: Negotiate signable threshold and test-administration clauses
task.where: Consortium working groups and member sign-off reviews
task.why: A signed spec beats an unwritten federal rule
task.how: Working group drafts, member ballots, published conformance criteria

actor: Technical director at an independent model evaluation organization
job: Building cyber, biological and alignment evaluations reproducible enough that instrument text can name them and an outsider can rerun them.
outcome: Named, versioned public evaluations that drafters cite instead of writing a threshold with no test behind it.
motivation: An origin-neutral gate only works if any lab's release can be measured by an outsider on the same battery.

task.who: Independent evaluation engineers, biosecurity advisors and cyber range operators
task.what: Ship versioned, reproducible pre-release risk evaluations
task.where: Public evaluation repositories and third-party audit engagements
task.why: Drafters need a battery an outsider can rerun
task.how: Open benchmark repos, held-out test sets, audited scoring protocols
